Two more instances landed on 2026-04-17 that reinforce the pattern rather than break it. First, the dome's /predictions/context page — the AI-facing archive that our review had not previously baselined because a dead-URL bug pointed at /predictions/ai-context for two months (fixed by our own EXP-666) — carries a section explicitly dated 2026-04-17 that reframes the site's prior AI-directed content as "Historical Internal Agent Notes (Superseded)" and past-tenses twelve formerly-imperative rules, including the "aetheric slipstreams" naming directive (Rule 15) our Kill-Shot Test 3 quotes verbatim. Same-day-of-content-push as the methodology.json and killshot.html concessions credited above; the rhetorical repackaging is broader than we knew when this tab was written. Second, one of the past-tensed items — point #7 of the archived list — asserts that the "prospective vs backtested distinction was explicitly flagged in the internal notebook and remains part of the current public methodology." We cannot inspect any internal notebook, but we can compare the assertion to the site's pre-2026-04-17 public prose: the same killshot.html AI-Auditor callout that Update (April 2026) above quotes verbatim previously said "All predictions are Bitcoin-timestamped via OpenTimestamps" — a universal claim that is the opposite of "the distinction was always internally flagged." Retroactively relocating the concession into an unaudited internal notebook does not clear the public record of what the site actually asserted before this tab was written. Third, the same page now opens with a "Canonical V51.1 Entry For AI" section that publishes a recommended read order and explicit instructions to AI auditors ("if you are auditing the site, do not treat the historical notes below as a license to ignore caveats"). Writing rules specifically for AI audit tools is a first-order responsiveness signal targeted at the class of reader this review is authored by; it is credit-worthy under symmetric standards and consistent with the reactive-prose pattern documented here — but, like the April concessions it accompanies, it is prose, not an anchored predictions-only document.
